title: Weights that can run code: pickle, safetensors, torch.load
hook: A .ckpt can hold a program that runs when you load it. See it happen, safely, and learn what stops it in ComfyUI, and what doesn't in a pack.

verified.claim: load_torch_file reads .safetensors and .sft through the safetensors path, and everything else with torch.load(..., weights_only=True). Its safe_load argument isn't consulted in this version.
A search of core's comfy, comfy_extras, app and top-level files found no weights_only=False and no pickle.load.
pickle.loads ran the payload. torch.load with weights_only=True refused it with UnpicklingError, and with weights_only=False ran it.
The Python docs say pickle can execute arbitrary code during unpickling, and the torch.load docs warn never to load data from an untrusted source.
The safetensors format is a length, a JSON header and raw data, and its README rates pickle as unsafe.
ComfyUI's security policy puts torch.load problems in old PyTorch versions out of scope and recommends recent versions.

unchecked: weights_only limits what the unpickler builds. We didn't try to attack it, and the PyTorch docs still warn against untrusted data, so don't treat it as a proof of safety.
Safetensors parsers can have bugs like any parser. We only say that its format has no pickle step.
What any given pack does: search it yourself. We name no pack here.
numpy.load with allow_pickle is listed from general knowledge of that option and not tested in the lab.
